rationale: This is a one-term swap (revt → revt−cogs) inside the archived "Knowledge Commercialization Claim Efficiency" expression, i.e. a cosmetic variant of an already-strong signal that also overlaps the archived R&D-adjusted gross-surplus coverage test, and the gross-profit numerator makes it partly a rescaled gross-profitability anomaly.

The added joint distress gate is a substantive state restriction rather than a variable swap and the signed-trend multiplier is internally consistent with the stated hypothesis, though using re/at as the filter and re/lt as the trend makes the two components mechanically related and the true incremental content over the archived replenishment signal may be small.

The refinement is motivated by a coherent diagnosis of the archived slope/alpha disagreement (debt volatility is only dangerous at high leverage) and the MIN construction matches the "jointly high" hypothesis, but adding a raw leverage rank risks importing a known leverage/distress effect and the short leg will be populated mainly by low-intangible firms rather than stable-financing ones.

This bolts a third MIN term onto an already-strong archived signal, and the specific term added (short-term debt intensity) has repeatedly failed in this archive ("Persistent Knowledge Duration Mismatch", "Cash-Confirmed Knowledge Rollover Risk"), so it reads as a low-information incremental variant rather than a new mechanism.

Replacing xrd/sale with TS_SUM(xrd,3)/at while leaving the rest of the archived "Cash-Sheltered Knowledge Volatility" expression untouched is exactly the kind of single-term cosmetic re-specification the objective warns against, and the flow-vs-stock distinction is highly collinear in practice.

It tests the untested positive-support side of recognized intangibles rather than repeating the archive's insolvency framing, but it is structurally parallel to Proposal 1 (so the two are partly redundant with each other), it inherits gross-profitability content, and the MIN gate means the short leg is dominated by low-intangible firms rather than intangible-heavy firms with weak surplus.
